guidance.procedure: Apply a separate predicate gate to every target; a clause responsive to one target does not answer its siblings. Technical-only scope requires exclusivity: mixed business, financial, personal, commercial, and technical categories oppose it, while generic information or communication-media language settles neither side. Express identification requires a condition covering all protected information; a broad definition, optional marking, or marking limited to one medium is insufficient. For oral inclusion, follow any contemporaneous designation and later written-confirmation conditions to completion. Agreement confidentiality requires operative coverage of the agreement, its existence, terms, discussions, or negotiations. Keep independent development and third-party receipt distinct from prior knowledge and public availability. After deciding relation from the whole source, make a second membership pass: collect every independently responsive definition, qualification, and exception with grammatical and numbered-list closure, but exclude headings, purpose recitals, content examples, and adjacent provisions that do not establish the tested predicate.

Analyze return, survival, and retention independently. For each operative clause record actor, act, object, trigger, coverage, duration, and exception. A termination-return duty requires termination, expiration, or an expressly equivalent ending event in that rule; a request-only obligation cannot borrow a trigger from another clause. Survival requires an express post-termination continuation or a duration tied to termination; an agreement term measured from effectiveness, severability, remedies, or continuing liability for earlier breaches is insufficient. For post-return possession, an express archival, backup, legal, audit, or dispute-retention exception can support permission, while an all-information or all-copies command with no-retention language can oppose it; a limited return command may leave the issue unsettled. Collect every independently responsive lifecycle rule and all spans completing its triggers, alternatives, coverage, and exceptions, without assigning return text to survival or retention merely because the provisions are adjacent.

Route evidence by the exact tested act: reverse engineer, solicit or contact, disclose, copy or reproduce, or use. Compare actor, object, modality, quantifiers, recipient class, conditions, and exceptions; do not transfer a restriction or permission between acts. Keep employee access separate from disclosure to consultants, advisers, agents, contractors, affiliates, or other outsiders. Expand a representative class only when the operative disclosure rule incorporates it, and preserve need-to-know, consent, and confidentiality conditions. For copying, require an express permission, prohibition, or operative exception concerning copying or reproduction; existing copies, copy markings, disclosure permission, and ownership do not suffice. For limited use, require an operative purpose restriction rather than a recital, disclosure rule, or copy ban. For solicitation and reverse engineering, require the named or materially equivalent act. Decide polarity from the complete rule, then cite all independently responsive provisions and every span completing split lists and incorporated conditions, excluding headings and neighboring duties that merely concern the same information.

Use two independent predicate gates. For compelled notice, first locate a legal, regulatory, judicial, subpoena, public-records, or comparable compelled-disclosure mechanism; then require an operative duty to notify, communicate with, or give the discloser an opportunity to object. A permission to disclose, a compelled-portion limit, or a section lead-in alone is not notice evidence. Scan separately for each mechanism and include every independently responsive notice rule, following any split sentence to completion. For no-license, require an express denial of a license, right, title, use right, proprietary interest, or intellectual-property right. Confidentiality, ownership, access, return, restricted use, or the absence of a grant cannot substitute for that denial. Include each independent denial and its grammatical completion, but exclude headings and adjacent provisions that merely describe ownership or permitted use.
